notes: Official EAN Clinical Fellowship page (ean.org) fetched successfully and reviewed. The fellowship is self-directed/portable: the applicant must first obtain a confirmed acceptance from an approved EAN host neurological department (EAN publishes the list of approved host departments as an Excel file) and must name a supervisor in the 'Acceptance by host department' form, where the supervisor is expected to have at least weekly direct contact with the applicant. EAN attaches no professor to the award itself, so no supervisor can be verified for the scheme. EAN's own published contacts are administrative (fellowship@ean.org / headoffice@ean.org). Side finding recorded for context only (not counted as a supervisor): from 2027 one 9-week Subrata and Sipra Chaudhuri Clinical Fellowship is endowed within the EAN clinical fellowship framework by Prof. Abhijit Chaudhuri, FEAN, and his family, but no supervisory or mentoring role is assigned to him by the programme.

Official ERS VISIT grant page (ersnet.org) fetched successfully. ERS states explicitly: 'The responsibility for identifying the most suitable institution and supervisor for the application rests entirely with the applicant. In all instances, the choice of the host institution remains the candidate's prerogative.' The grant funds a self-nominated visit of up to one month to an institution of the applicant's choosing; no supervisor, lab or faculty member is attached to the scheme by ERS. Host Institution Invitation Form and Home Supervisor Support Form are blank templates completed by the applicant's chosen hosts.

Official EAN Research Fellowship page (ean.org) fetched successfully. The research must be carried out at a European academic neurological department outside the applicant's country of residence chosen by the applicant, and the letter of acceptance from the host department chair must name the proposed mentor at the host institution. EAN reviews the 'proposed host (department, supervisor)' but attaches no professor to the award, so no supervisor can be verified for the scheme. EAN contacts are administrative (fellowship@ean.org / headoffice@ean.org).

notes: GIAS is an independent institute established by the Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation (gulbenkian.pt/gias). Fellowships are self-directed research residencies: fellows pursue projects of their own choosing with 'minimal regular obligations' and the institute provides no formal supervision, so the professors listed are the programme's leadership/selection faculty rather than PhD supervisors. Verified on official gulbenkian.pt pages: (1) Miguel Tamen, founding director of GIAS and Professor of Literary Theory at the University of Lisbon; (2) Lorraine Daston, Director Emerita of the Max Planck Institute for the History of Science, Berlin; (3) Sofia Miguens, Professor of Philosophy at the University of Porto, who leads the MLA (Mind, Language and Action) research team. All three are members of the six-person GIAS Advisory Board that selects each fellow cohort. Other board members verified but not listed (max 3 per scholarship): Brett Bourbon (University of Dallas), Caroline A. Jones, Mark Lilla, Ricardo Soares de Oliveira (Sciences Po Paris / University of Oxford). No institutional email addresses are published on any of these official pages, so official_email is null and official_email_verified is false everywhere; GIAS programme contact published on the call page is the generic gias@gulbenkian.pt (not a personal address and therefore not recorded as a professor email).

Official FWO Junior Postdoctoral Fellowship page (fwo.be) fetched successfully. This is a Flemish government research-council personal fellowship: the candidate must first 'find a supervisor at a Flemish host institution' (article 3 of the regulations on postdoctoral researchers) and that supervisor writes the mandatory letter of recommendation. FWO attaches no named professor, host or lab to the call (from the 2027 call a supervisor may support at most five applications), so no supervisor can be verified. FWO partners referenced on the page (Plantentuin Meise, VITO, Flanders Hydraulics, Suzanne Duchesne Fund via King Baudouin Foundation, L'Oreal-UNESCO) are funding partners, not supervising faculty; FWO's own contacts are administrative (FWOhelpdesk@fwo.be, account administrators).

Official Toronto Metropolitan University scholarships and awards page (torontomu.ca) fetched successfully. ISLA - Fall (CAD 10,000, up to 53 recipients, entrance-only and non-renewable, application via AwardSpring) is an undergraduate entrance scholarship for international students entering post-secondary study for the first time; it carries no research component, no supervisor and no attached department. The award is administered by the university's Student Awards and Scholarships Office / International Enrolment Office (generic contact awards@torontomu.ca), so no professor can be associated with it.

Official Tecnologico de Monterrey scholarships page (tec.mx/es/profesional/becas) fetched successfully. The Beca al Talento Academico is an undergraduate entrance scholarship for new entrants to professional (licenciatura) programmes starting August-December, awarded 20-60% of tuition on the basis of secondary-school average and the PAA admissions test, and valid for the admitted campus. Selection is made by the Admissions 'Comite de Becas'; the scholarship has no research or supervision component and no attached faculty member, so no supervisor can be verified.
